#### By country and crop

To split the loss by crop, we ran the Roberts & Schlenker shock on palm alone and on soybeans alone. Palm accounts for `r fmt0(100 * crop_split[["palm"]] / sum(crop_split))`% of the additional loss and soybeans for `r fmt0(100 * crop_split[["soy"]] / sum(crop_split))`%. The two single-crop runs add up to the combined run to within `r formatC(abs(interaction_pct), format = "f", digits = 2)`%, so the interaction between them is negligible.

```{r}
#| label: forest-loss-country-chart
#| fig-width: 7.5
#| fig-height: 5.2

top_n <- 12
top_countries <- rs_final$country[seq_len(top_n)]
other_label <- sprintf("Other %d countries", sum(rs_final$carbon_loss > 0) - top_n)

crop_by_country <- country_final |>
  dplyr::filter(scenario %in% c("vo_rs_palm", "vo_rs_soy")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    label = ifelse(country %in% top_countries, country, other_label),
    crop = ifelse(scenario == "vo_rs_palm", "Oil palm", "Soybeans")
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarise(mt = sum(carbon_loss) / 1e6, .by = c(label, crop)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(label = factor(label, levels = rev(c(top_countries, other_label))))
bar_totals <- crop_by_country |> dplyr::summarise(mt = sum(mt), .by = label)

ggplot2::ggplot(crop_by_country, ggplot2::aes(mt, label)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(
    ggplot2::aes(fill = crop),
    position = ggplot2::position_stack(reverse = TRUE), # palm first, from zero
    width = 0.62, colour = col_surface, linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(data = bar_totals, ggplot2::aes(label = fmt0(mt)), hjust = -0.2, size = 3.2, colour = "#0b0b0b") +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = col_crop, name = NULL) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma(), expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Additional forest carbon loss by country and crop",
    subtitle = "Roberts & Schlenker scenario, full horizon",
    x = expression("Mt CO"[2]),
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_report() +
  ggplot2::theme(panel.grid.major.y = ggplot2::element_blank())
```

```{r}
#| label: forest-loss-country-table

country_table <- country_final |>
  dplyr::filter(carbon_loss > 0) |>
  dplyr::select(country, scenario, carbon_loss, area_loss, area_bau, share)
by_scenario <- function(scn, ...) {
  country_table |> dplyr::filter(scenario == scn) |> dplyr::select(country, ...)
}
country_table <- by_scenario("vo_rs", carbon_loss, area_loss, area_bau, share) |>
  dplyr::left_join(by_scenario("vo_rs_palm", carbon_palm = carbon_loss), by = "country") |>
  dplyr::left_join(by_scenario("vo_rs_soy", carbon_soy = carbon_loss), by = "country") |>
  dplyr::left_join(by_scenario("vo_rs_model", carbon_high = carbon_loss), by = "country") |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    country,
    carbon_mt = carbon_loss / 1e6,
    palm_mt = dplyr::coalesce(carbon_palm, 0) / 1e6,
    soy_mt = dplyr::coalesce(carbon_soy, 0) / 1e6,
    area_kha = area_loss / 1e3,
    share_pct = 100 * share,
    pct_of_bau_area = 100 * area_loss / area_bau,
    carbon_mt_high = dplyr::coalesce(carbon_high, 0) / 1e6
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(carbon_mt))

DT::datatable(
  country_table,
  rownames = FALSE,
  colnames = c(
    "Country",
    "R&S: Mt CO₂",
    "of which palm",
    "of which soybeans",
    "R&S: thousand ha",
    "R&S: share of total (%)",
    "R&S: % of country's BAU forest",
    "Model supply: Mt CO₂"
  ),
  caption = "Cumulative additional forest loss relative to BAU over the full horizon, by country. Palm and soybean columns are the single-crop runs.",
  options = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE)
) |>
  DT::formatRound(c("carbon_mt", "palm_mt", "soy_mt", "area_kha", "share_pct", "pct_of_bau_area", "carbon_mt_high"), digits = 1)
```

`r sum(rs_final$carbon_loss > 0)` countries lose some additional forest, but `r rs_final$country[1]`, `r rs_final$country[2]` and `r rs_final$country[3]` account for `r fmt0(100 * sum(rs_final$share[1:3]))`% of the total. Only cells that grow oil palm or soybeans respond, because those are the only prices that change.

Because cleared forest never grows back, BAU can later clear forest that a shocked run cleared earlier. In Malaysia the additional loss peaks at `r fmt0(mys$peak / 1e6)` Mt CO₂ in model year `r mys$peak_year` and falls to `r fmt0(mys$final / 1e6)` Mt CO₂ by `r final_year`, and `r n_narrowing` countries drop more than 5% below their peak. Globally the additional loss is still rising at the end of the run. The ILUC estimates below only count loss within the accounting period, so this late catch-up does not affect them.

### ILUC carbon intensity {#sec-results-iluc}

```{r}
#| label: iluc-table

iluc_wide <- function(scn) iluc[iluc$scenario == scn, ]
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    "Accounting period (years)" = accounting_years,
    "R&S: additional loss (Gt CO₂)" = iluc_wide("vo_rs")$carbon_loss / 1e9,
    "R&S: ILUC (g CO₂/MJ)" = iluc_wide("vo_rs")$g_per_mj,
    "R&S: VO-RD total (g CO₂e/MJ)" = vord_direct_ci + iluc_wide("vo_rs")$g_per_mj,
    "Model supply: additional loss (Gt CO₂)" = iluc_wide("vo_rs_model")$carbon_loss / 1e9,
    "Model supply: ILUC (g CO₂/MJ)" = iluc_wide("vo_rs_model")$g_per_mj,
    "Model supply: VO-RD total (g CO₂e/MJ)" = vord_direct_ci + iluc_wide("vo_rs_model")$g_per_mj,
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  digits = c(0, 2, 1, 1, 2, 1, 1),
  caption = paste0(
    "ILUC carbon intensity of VO-RD for each accounting period, using ", fmt1(vord_mj_2035 / 1e12),
    " EJ of VO-RD a year. VO-RD total adds the direct 42.3 g CO₂e/MJ [@seber2025, p. 6]; ",
    "the fossil baseline is 93.3 [@seber2025, p. 1]."
  )
)
```

Over the `r headline_years`-year headline period, the ILUC estimate is `r fmt1(il("vo_rs", 25))` g CO₂/MJ in the Roberts & Schlenker scenario and `r fmt1(il("vo_rs_model", 25))` with the land-use model's own supply elasticity. The 30-year values, `r fmt1(il("vo_rs", 30))` and `r fmt1(il("vo_rs_model", 30))`, are the ones to set against the 62 g CO₂e/MJ ICCT has used, since that number comes from a 2020–2050 window. Both benchmarks, ICCT's 62 and Chen et al.'s 84.1, are ILUC alone, so they compare with these values and not with the totals that include VO-RD's direct `r vord_direct_ci` g CO₂e/MJ. Our estimates count only forest biomass carbon, while Chen et al. also count peat (614 of their 1,086 Tg CO₂e) and soil carbon [@chen2026, Table 1, p. 13], so on that count ours are too low.

```{r}
#| label: iluc-country-chart
#| fig-width: 7.5
#| fig-height: 5

# Contributions to the headline ILUC estimate: each country's additional loss after
# headline_years years in the palm-only and soy-only runs, in g CO2 per MJ of VO-RD.
iluc_year <- min(lum$year) + headline_years
iluc_by_country <- lum |>
  dplyr::filter(year == iluc_year, scenario %in% c("bau", "vo_rs_palm", "vo_rs_soy")) |>
  dplyr::select(country, scenario, forest_carbon_tco2) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    palm = forest_carbon_tco2[scenario == "bau"] - forest_carbon_tco2[scenario == "vo_rs_palm"],
    soy = forest_carbon_tco2[scenario == "bau"] - forest_carbon_tco2[scenario == "vo_rs_soy"],
    .by = country
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    dplyr::across(c(palm, soy), \(x) x * 1e6 / (headline_years * vord_mj_2035)),
    total = palm + soy
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(total))

iluc_top_n <- 10
iluc_top <- iluc_by_country$country[seq_len(iluc_top_n)]
iluc_other <- sprintf("Other %d countries", sum(iluc_by_country$total > 0) - iluc_top_n)
iluc_plot <- iluc_by_country |>
  dplyr::mutate(label = ifelse(country %in% iluc_top, country, iluc_other)) |>
  dplyr::summarise(`Oil palm` = sum(palm), Soybeans = sum(soy), .by = label)
iluc_plot <- rbind(
  data.frame(label = iluc_plot$label, crop = "Oil palm", g_per_mj = iluc_plot$`Oil palm`),
  data.frame(label = iluc_plot$label, crop = "Soybeans", g_per_mj = iluc_plot$Soybeans)
)
iluc_plot$label <- factor(iluc_plot$label, levels = rev(c(iluc_top, iluc_other)))
iluc_totals <- iluc_plot |> dplyr::summarise(g_per_mj = sum(g_per_mj), .by = label)

ggplot2::ggplot(iluc_plot, ggplot2::aes(g_per_mj, label)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(
    ggplot2::aes(fill = crop),
    position = ggplot2::position_stack(reverse = TRUE),
    width = 0.62, colour = col_surface, linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(data = iluc_totals, ggplot2::aes(label = fmt1(g_per_mj)), hjust = -0.2, size = 3.2, colour = "#0b0b0b") +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = col_crop, name = NULL) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Contributions to the ILUC estimate by country and crop",
    subtitle = paste0("Roberts & Schlenker scenario, ", headline_years, "-year accounting period"),
    x = expression("g CO"[2] * " per MJ of VO-RD"),
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_report() +
  ggplot2::theme(panel.grid.major.y = ggplot2::element_blank())
```

`r iluc_by_country$country[1]` and `r iluc_by_country$country[2]` contribute `r fmt1(sum(iluc_by_country$total[1:2]))` of the `r fmt1(sum(iluc_by_country$total))` g CO₂/MJ, and the palm price increase accounts for `r fmt0(100 * sum(iluc_by_country$palm) / sum(iluc_by_country$total))`% of the total.

## Caveats {#sec-caveats}

What the estimates leave out or assume:

- Only forest carbon is counted. Peat, soil carbon and lost future sequestration are not. Peat was 614 of the 1,086 Tg CO₂e in Chen et al.'s estimate [@chen2026, Table 1, p. 13], so this matters most for Indonesia and Malaysia. This understates ILUC.
- Rapeseed and sunflower are not in the model, which also understates ILUC.
- The price shock comes from a linear approximation applied to a very large demand shift (63% of the market). The true price response is probably larger.
- The soybean price change uses an accounting share (0.353), not an estimated market response.
- We make no adjustment for soy meal in the oil-price shock, which overstates it.
- Our primary price shock uses Roberts & Schlenker's supply elasticity of 0.10, about `r fmt0(signif(0.10 / eps_model("vegetable_oil"), 1))` times the land-use model's own one-year supply elasticity of `r formatC(eps_model("vegetable_oil"), digits = 2, format = "fg")` ([Methods](#sec-model-supply)). So the price we give the model is not the one its own supply response would produce. The alternative scenario uses the model's own elasticity. That makes the two steps consistent, but it assumes that only new cropland on cleared forest adds supply, which inflates the price shock.
- Roberts & Schlenker's elasticities are for the world market in staple calories (maize, wheat, rice and soybeans), not for vegetable oils.
- One global price change applies in every country, as if supply and the pass-through of world prices to farmers were the same everywhere. They are not, so the split of the loss across countries is less certain than the global total. Country effects are held at their 2016–2020 average, and the model pools some small neighboring countries into regions. Each cell gets the crop mix of a broad GAEZ zone, so our palm price shock is spread thinly in the palm frontiers and reaches much of Central Africa; this probably explains why the Democratic Republic of the Congo ranks first ([Appendix C](#sec-crop-mix)).
- Prices jump once in the first model year and stay there, and cleared forest never grows back (see [Methods](#sec-land-use-model)).

## Use of generative AI

We used Claude (Anthropic, model Opus 5.5) through Claude Code as a coding and writing assistant. It drafted and edited much of the R code, including the changes to the land-use model in [Appendix A](#sec-lum-changes), and much of this report's prose, and it helped find and check sources. GitHub Copilot's coding agent set up the initial Quarto report and GitHub Pages workflow. We set the research question and scenarios, chose the data sources and key assumptions, and reviewed the code and text. The AI tools are not authors, and we are responsible for all code, analysis and conclusions. The AI tools produced no data or results: every number, figure and table is computed by the code in the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/emlab-ucsb/marine-biofuel-iluc-prototype) when the report is built.

## Appendix A: Changes to the land-use model code {#sec-lum-changes}

This lists every change we made to the emLab land-use model to run the price scenarios, for the model's authors to review. Starting point: upstream `emlab-ucsb/land-based-solutions`, `r/robert_test/parallelization/` at commit `e207c2b` (31 July 2026), copied to `r/land_use_model/` (see `r/land_use_model/PROVENANCE.md`). Anything not listed here is unchanged.

**Unchanged:** `simulation_functions.R` (including `update_revenues()` and `simulate_10_dt()`), `packages.R`, `r/directories.R` (now only read from, via `paths.R`), the deforestation model and its coefficients, and the fixed-effect construction (pixel FEs, the 2016–2020 country-year FE window, asymmetric-information FEs).

**All scripts**

1. `r/robert_test/parallelization/` → `r/land_use_model/` in every `here::here()` path.

**New file: `paths.R`**

2. Defines the input root `input_wdir`, read via `r/directories.R` as `{data_directory}/parallelized` and treated as read-only, and the output root `wdir`, the repo's git-ignored `land_use_model_runs/`. It stops if `wdir` is inside any Nextcloud folder or inside the inputs. This is so our outputs can't sync over the shared Nextcloud files of the same name.

**`01_prepare_data.R`**

3. Carbon price fixed at 0: `CP_LIST` (10 carbon prices) replaced by `CP <- 0`.
4. New input `PRICE_SHOCKS` (Section 1): % price change per shocked crop, one element per scenario, with `bau` first and unshocked. Scenarios: `bau`; `vo_20pct` (smoke test, `Oil, palm` and `Soybeans` both +20%); `vo_rs` and `vo_rs_model`, built from the 2035 shocks read from `data/derived/vegetable_oil_price_shock_2035.csv` (`pct_delta_p_rs`: Roberts & Schlenker's supply and demand elasticities; `pct_delta_p_rs_model`: their demand elasticity with this model's own supply elasticity from `00d_supply_curve.R`), with `Oil, palm` taking the full shock and `Soybeans` taking `SOY_OIL_VALUE_SHARE` (0.353, Janzen & Wang 2025) of it; and `vo_rs_palm` and `vo_rs_soy`, the `vo_rs` shock applied to one crop at a time, for crop attribution. Sources for every number are in [Methods](#sec-mapping). (`vo_rs` and `vo_rs_model` replaced `vo_central`, which used Chen et al.'s elasticities, and `vo_high`, which was the same shock as `vo_rs`.)
5. New Section 2b: expands `PRICE_SHOCKS` into `PRICE_SCENARIOS`, one full 17-crop price vector per scenario, starting from the `CPrice == 0` rows of `final_prices_allcp`. Writes `price_scenarios.csv`. Stops if a shocked crop isn't in the model, or if any crop in `endo_input_data` has no price.
6. Section 6: `update_revenues()` runs once per price scenario (`revenue_<scenario>` columns) instead of once per carbon price (`revenue_cp<P>`). BAU revenue is computed the same way instead of being taken from `data_past$revenue`, so every scenario uses one formula. The two BAU versions agree to ~1e-12, and the script prints that check on every run.
7. Section 8: chunk files carry `revenue_<scenario>` columns in place of `revenue_cp0` and `revenue_cp<P>`.
8. Section 8: the per-pixel attributes file `grid_smry.csv` also carries `lat` and `lon`, for mapping.
9. Section 11: `model_params.rds` stores `cp` and `price_scenarios` in place of `cp_list`.
10. Paths come from `paths.R` instead of the hard-coded `/Users/rheilmayr/Nextcloud/...` `wdir`, which upstream used for both inputs and outputs.

**`02_run_simulations.R`**

11. The 38 distinct simulations (56 labeled blocks across endog/exog, fi/fi_bl_vp/ai_bl_vp and carbon price) are replaced by one `simulate_10_dt()` run per price scenario, at `cp = 0` with `pixel_fe`. This is the same construction as upstream's `endog_fi_blvp` runs, $D(0, V(P))$, with scenario prices in place of carbon-price equilibrium prices.
12. Output parquet columns are `scn, pixel_id, year, biomass` (upstream: `crp_price, cprice, pixel_id, year, info, biomass`). The row-count check is now pixels × scenarios × years.
13. Paths come from `paths.R`, as in `01`.

**Disabled scripts**

14. `00_generate_sample_data.R`, `00c_run_cobweb.R`, `01b_prepare_uncertainty_draws.R`, `02b_run_simulations_uncertainty.R`, and `03_aggregate_results.R` through `09_conceptual_diagrams.R` (including `03b`) have a `stop()` as their first line. They still expect upstream's carbon-price outputs and use upstream's hard-coded paths, which on a colleague's machine point at the shared Nextcloud folder. `00` and `00c` write into `1_input/` itself. Each `stop()` comes out only when that script is adapted to `paths.R`.

**New file: `03_summarise_results.R`**

15. Reduces `02`'s per-pixel results to two files for the report, pairing each result file with its chunk file for each pixel's `country` and `CF`:
    - `data/derived/land_use_country_results.csv.gz`: country × scenario × year totals of forest carbon (`sum(biomass)`, t CO₂) and forest area (`sum(biomass / CF)`, ha, using upstream's `ha_per_pixel = CF_pix / CF`).
    - `data/derived/land_use_grid_loss.csv.gz`: per 0.5° grid square (from `grid_smry.csv` coordinates), 2020 forest carbon and final-year additional loss relative to BAU for each scenario.

    Stops if BAU 2020 forest carbon doesn't match `01`'s `grid_smry.csv`, or if any scenario's gridded loss doesn't sum to its country-level loss.

**`run_pipeline.R`**

16. `STAGES` runs `01` → `02` → `03_summarise_results.R`; upstream stages `03`–`07` are commented out.

**New file: `00d_supply_curve.R`**

17. Traces the model's own supply curves ([Methods](#sec-model-supply)). The report turns the one-year vegetable-oil curve into the supply elasticity behind `vo_rs_model`, so the order of a full update is `00d` → render the report (which writes the price shocks) → `run_pipeline.R` → render again. It is not in `STAGES`; like upstream's `00c_run_cobweb.R`, it is run by hand, and it doesn't depend on `PRICE_SHOCKS`.
    - It reads the same inputs as `01` and prepares them the same way: 2020 pixels, `alpha` and `beta`, pixel FEs, and 2016–2020 country FEs.
    - For each price change in `PCT_CHANGES` (−50% to +1,500%), it changes the palm price, the soybean price, or both (soybeans by `SOY_OIL_VALUE_SHARE` times the palm change). It then runs `simulate_10_dt()` for 25 years at `cp = 0` with `pixel_fe`.
    - Extra forest cleared relative to BAU becomes extra production through upstream's conversion in `endog_prices()`: cleared 30 m pixels × `ha_pixel` × `def_for_ag_share` × `harvested_share_gaez` × `m3_yield_ton_per_ha`, with NAs counted as zero. The same sum without `def_for_ag_share` is reported as an upper bound.
    - Revenue at each price is BAU revenue plus multiples of the revenue change from a +100% palm step and a +100% soybean step, each from `update_revenues()`. This is exact because revenue is linear in each price, and it avoids rerunning `update_revenues()` for every price vector.
    - It writes `data/derived/land_use_supply_curve.csv`: extra forest loss and extra palm-oil and soybean production by experiment, price change, and years after the change (1, 5, 10, 25).

**Verification** (200-pixel sample inputs, `1_input/smpl`):

- BAU emissions per pixel, annualized the same way as `03`'s `bl_emit_co2_y`, match upstream's reference run (`5_validation/sim_results_exog_ref_smpl.csv`) to within 0.003% for all 201 pixels.
- `vo_20pct` biomass is never higher than BAU, and is lower in the 110 of 201 pixels that grow palm or soy.

**Verification** (full inputs, `1_input/full`, 1,450,769 pixels):

- BAU revenue recomputed with `update_revenues()` matches upstream's `data_past$revenue` to within 7e-12.
- At every pixel, biomass in 2035 and 2171 is never higher under a shock than under BAU, and never higher under `vo_rs_model` than under `vo_rs`. By 2171, 687,384 pixels have less forest under `vo_rs_model` than under BAU.
- `vo_rs_palm` and `vo_rs_soy` sum to `vo_rs` to within 0.11% of its additional loss 15 years after the shock, and to within 0.02% at the end of the horizon.
- `03_summarise_results.R`: BAU 2020 forest carbon summed by country equals `01`'s per-pixel 2020 biomass, and each scenario's gridded loss equals its country-level loss.
- `00d_supply_curve.R`: the revenue shortcut matches a direct `update_revenues()` call (palm +150%, soybeans +50%) to within 1e-10. Its BAU and +20% runs reproduce `02`'s global forest carbon 1, 5, 10 and 25 years after the shock to within 1e-9. `ha_pixel` equals upstream's `CF_pix / CF` to within 1e-13. The 57 price-change simulations take 168 s after the inputs load.
- Runtime on a 64 GB laptop, six scenarios: `01` 238 s (peak memory ~27 GB), `02` 142 s, `03_summarise_results.R` 43 s.

## Appendix B: Results of the +20% test run {#sec-test-run}

This is the first run the model's authors asked for: oil palm and soybean prices both up 20% (soybeans by the full 20%, without the oil-share adjustment), at a zero carbon price, with everything else as in [Methods](#sec-land-use-model). It is a check on how the model responds, not a policy scenario.

```{r}
#| label: test-run-global

test_global <- lum |>
  dplyr::filter(scenario %in% c("bau", "vo_20pct")) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    carbon = sum(forest_carbon_tco2),
    area = sum(forest_area_ha),
    .by = c(scenario, year)
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(scenario, year)
test_bau <- test_global[test_global$scenario == "bau", ]
test_shock <- test_global[test_global$scenario == "vo_20pct", ]
stopifnot(identical(test_bau$year, test_shock$year))

base_year <- min(lum$year)
test_rows <- match(c(base_year + 1, 2035, 2050, final_year), test_bau$year)
bau_loss <- test_bau$carbon[test_bau$year == base_year] - test_bau$carbon[test_rows]
extra_loss <- test_bau$carbon[test_rows] - test_shock$carbon[test_rows]

knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    "Years after shock" = test_bau$year[test_rows] - base_year,
    "BAU forest carbon loss (Gt CO₂)" = bau_loss / 1e9,
    "Additional loss, +20% (Gt CO₂)" = extra_loss / 1e9,
    "Additional loss, +20% (Mha)" = (test_bau$area[test_rows] - test_shock$area[test_rows]) / 1e6,
    "Additional as % of BAU loss (CO₂)" = 100 * extra_loss / bau_loss,
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  digits = c(0, 1, 3, 2, 2),
  caption = "+20% test run: cumulative forest carbon loss under BAU and additional loss from the price increase, all countries."
)
```

BAU loses `r fmt1(bau_loss[1] / 1e9)` Gt CO₂ of forest carbon in the first year, close to the ~4.2 Gt first-year figure noted in a comment in upstream's `01_prepare_data.R` (Section 5). The 20% price increase adds `r fmt1(100 * extra_loss[2] / bau_loss[2])`% to BAU's cumulative loss over 15 years. That share shrinks over longer horizons because BAU loss keeps accumulating while the extra loss from the shock levels off.

```{r}
#| label: test-run-countries

test_countries <- lum |>
  dplyr::filter(scenario %in% c("bau", "vo_20pct"), year %in% c(2035, final_year)) |>
  dplyr::select(country, scenario, year, forest_carbon_tco2) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    extra_mt = (forest_carbon_tco2[scenario == "bau"] - forest_carbon_tco2[scenario == "vo_20pct"]) / 1e6,
    .by = c(country, year)
  )
test_top <- dplyr::inner_join(
  test_countries |> dplyr::filter(year == 2035) |> dplyr::select(country, extra_15 = extra_mt),
  test_countries |> dplyr::filter(year == final_year) |> dplyr::select(country, extra_full = extra_mt),
  by = "country"
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(share_pct = 100 * extra_full / sum(extra_full)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(extra_full)) |>
  utils::head(10)

knitr::kable(
  test_top,
  digits = 1,
  col.names = c("Country", "Additional loss, 15 years (Mt CO₂)", "Additional loss, full horizon (Mt CO₂)", "Share of global (%)"),
  caption = "+20% test run: the ten countries with the largest additional forest carbon loss."
)
```

## Appendix C: The model's crop mix and our crop-specific price shocks {#sec-crop-mix}

This note is for the authors of emLab's land-use model. We want to confirm that we are using the model correctly, and we are not suggesting any change to it. The model was built for carbon prices, which compete with a cell's total agricultural revenue. We use it to shock just two crops, palm oil and soybeans, so how it splits a cell's revenue among crops matters much more for us.

```{r}
#| label: crop-mix-data

# Written by r/audit_crop_mix.R from the model's inputs (read-only) and this repository's model run.
cm_num <- utils::read.csv(file.path("data", "derived", "crop_mix_numbers.csv"))
cm <- function(metric) cm_num$value[cm_num$metric == metric]
cm_regions <- utils::read.csv(file.path("data", "derived", "crop_mix_regions.csv"))
cm_countries <- utils::read.csv(file.path("data", "derived", "crop_mix_countries.csv"))
cm_grid <- utils::read.csv(file.path("data", "derived", "crop_mix_grid.csv.gz"))
pct <- function(x) paste0(formatC(100 * x, format = "f", digits = 1), "%")

# Indonesia and Malaysia, +1% palm price, first year: the model and Chen et al. (2026).
im_palm_share_of_cleared <- cm("im_model_extra_palm_t") / cm("im_model_palm_t_if_all_cleared_land_were_palm")
im_chen_palm_t <- cm("im_chen_extra_clearing_ha") * cm("im_model_palm_yield_t_per_ha")
im_model_ha_per_cell_per_1000 <- (cm("im_model_extra_clearing_ha") / cm("im_cells")) /
  (cm("im_model_d_rev_annual_crop_mix") / 1000)
```

### What we found

- **The crop mix is set per zone.** Each cell's revenue (`update_revenues()`) and crop production (`endog_prices()`) weight crops by `harvested_share_gaez`. That share is the same for every cell with the same `gaez` value (`r fmt0(cm("gaez_zones"))` values, such as `54_Europe`). We assume this gives forest cells, which have little cropland of their own, the crop mix of the wider area.
- **For palm and soybeans, that mix differs a lot from the frontiers' own.** We look at four frontiers where palm or soybeans already make up much of the cropland: Riau, a province in central Sumatra, Indonesia, and Sabah and Sarawak, the Malaysian states on Borneo, for palm; and Mato Grosso, Brazil, and the Paraguayan Chaco for soybeans. For each crop's actual share of a cell's cropland we use the inputs' `m3_harvested_area_ha` column. We assume it comes from M3 [@monfreda2008], a global map of harvested area and yield for 175 crops around 2000, on a grid of about 10 km. In Riau, palm is `r pct(cm_regions$palm_share_m3[1])` of M3 harvested area but `r pct(cm_regions$palm_share_median[1])` of the model's crop mix, and no cell anywhere gets more than `r pct(cm("palm_share_max"))`. Palm is also more than 5% of the crop mix in `r fmt0(cm_countries$cells_palm_over_5pct[cm_countries$country == "Democratic Republic of the Congo"])` cells in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (table and map below).
- **So, as we use the model, palm responds little to its own price.** In Indonesia and Malaysia, a 1% palm price rise produces `r fmt0(im_chen_palm_t / cm("im_model_extra_palm_t"))` times less palm oil from forest in the first year than Chen et al.'s econometric estimate implies [@chen2026, p. 5]. The model responds at least as strongly to revenue: about `r fmt0(im_model_ha_per_cell_per_1000)` ha cleared per cell per \$1,000/ha, against Chen et al.'s 9.3. The gap comes from palm's small share of revenue and of the cleared land.
- **This drives two of our results.** The supply elasticity we read off the model (`r fmt_eps(eps_model("vegetable_oil"))`, against Roberts & Schlenker's 0.10) is tiny, and so the price shock built on it (`r fmt0(shock_2035$pct_delta_p_rs_model)`%) is huge. It also probably explains why the Democratic Republic of the Congo has the most additional loss in our results.

```{r}
#| label: crop-mix-regions

frontier_crop <- c("Palm", "Palm", "Soybeans", "Soybeans")
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    "Frontier" = sub(" \\(.*", "", cm_regions$region),
    "Crop" = frontier_crop,
    "Share of crop mix, model" = pct(ifelse(frontier_crop == "Palm", cm_regions$palm_share_median, cm_regions$soy_share_median)),
    "Share of harvested area, M3" = pct(ifelse(frontier_crop == "Palm", cm_regions$palm_share_m3, cm_regions$soy_share_m3)),
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  align = "llrr",
  caption = paste(
    "The frontier crop's share in four frontiers. Model: harvested_share_gaez (median cell).",
    "M3: the crop's share of all 17 crops' M3 harvested area (m3_harvested_area_ha) in the same cells."
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    "+1% palm price, first year" = c("Extra forest cleared (ha)", "Share of it counted as palm", "Extra palm oil (t)"),
    "Model" = c(fmt0(cm("im_model_extra_clearing_ha")), pct(im_palm_share_of_cleared), fmt0(cm("im_model_extra_palm_t"))),
    "Implied by Chen et al." = c(fmt0(cm("im_chen_extra_clearing_ha")), "100%", fmt0(im_chen_palm_t)),
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  align = "lrr",
  caption = paste0(
    "Indonesia and Malaysia. Chen et al.: +9.3 ha of forest-to-palm conversion per cell per \\$1,000/ha of annual ",
    "attainable revenue, at their mean revenue (\\$1,933/ha) over 32,394 cells. Model: simulate_10_dt()'s first-year ",
    "deforestation and endog_prices()'s production in its ", fmt0(cm("im_cells")), " cells there. Both use the model's palm yield (",
    formatC(cm("im_model_palm_yield_t_per_ha"), format = "f", digits = 1), " t/ha)."
  )
)
```

```{r}
#| label: crop-mix-map
#| column: body-outset
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8.6
#| fig-cap: "Palm's share of the crop mix in each 0.5° square: as the model uses it (harvested_share_gaez, averaged over the square's cells), and from M3 harvested area in the same cells."

share_classes <- c("0", "< 1%", "1–5%", "5–10%", "10–20%", "20–50%", "≥ 50%", "No M3 cropland")
share_class <- function(x) {
  cls <- as.character(cut(x, c(0, 0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.50, Inf), right = FALSE, labels = share_classes[2:7]))
  factor(ifelse(is.na(x), "No M3 cropland", ifelse(x == 0, "0", cls)), levels = share_classes)
}
map_panels <- c(model = "Crop mix the model uses (harvested_share_gaez, set per GAEZ zone)", m3 = "M3 harvested area in the same cells")
palm_map <- rbind(
  data.frame(lon = cm_grid$lon, lat = cm_grid$lat, panel = map_panels[["model"]], class = share_class(cm_grid$palm_share_model)),
  data.frame(lon = cm_grid$lon, lat = cm_grid$lat, panel = map_panels[["m3"]], class = share_class(cm_grid$palm_share_m3))
)
palm_map$panel <- factor(palm_map$panel, levels = map_panels)

ggplot2::ggplot() +
  ggplot2::geom_polygon(
    data = basemap,
    ggplot2::aes(lon, lat, group = piece, subgroup = ring),
    fill = col_land, colour = col_surface, linewidth = 0.2
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_tile(data = palm_map, ggplot2::aes(lon, lat, fill = class), width = 0.5, height = 0.5) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 1) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
    values = stats::setNames(c("#e6e4dc", map_ramp(6), "#a9a79f"), share_classes),
    breaks = share_classes,
    name = "Palm share of the crop mix",
    drop = FALSE,
    guide = ggplot2::guide_legend(nrow = 1, title.position = "top", label.position = "bottom", keywidth = ggplot2::unit(1.6, "cm"), keyheight = ggplot2::unit(0.3, "cm"))
  ) +
  ggplot2::coord_quickmap(xlim = c(-180, 180), ylim = c(-57, 84), expand = FALSE) +
  theme_map() +
  ggplot2::theme(strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(colour = "#0b0b0b", hjust = 0))
```

Until we hear back, we treat the model-derived supply elasticity and the scenario built on it as unreliable. We also caution against reading our country results as a map of where palm-driven deforestation would happen.

### Our questions

1. Is a price change for individual crops, like ours, a use of the model you would expect to work, given that the crop mix is set per GAEZ zone?
2. Should we simply use a published, market-wide supply elasticity (Roberts & Schlenker's 0.10, as in our primary scenario) instead of estimating our own from the model? If so, we will drop the scenario that uses the model's own.
3. Given the crop mix, would you report our results by country, or only as global totals?

`r/audit_crop_mix.R` reproduces every number here from the unmodified inputs and this repository's model run.
